RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the August 31, 2007/Bhadrapada 9, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs,
Food and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare;
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
82
High speed trains
*261. DR. K. KESHAVA RAO: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
is considering to introduce high speed trains
which would run at the speed of 350
kilometre per hour across the country;
(b) if so, the details of the routes and
names of the States which have expressed
interest in the high speed lines;
(c) whether any request has been
received from the Government of Andhra
Pradesh in this regard;
(d) if so, the response of his Ministry;
and
(e) by when the proposal would be
taken up?
Failure of PDS
*262. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) the quantum of wheat, rice, sugar,
kerosene, etc. fixed per person per BPL/
APL card, through PDS;
(b) whether it is sufficient;
(c) the details of malpractices in PDS;
(d) the cases detected/registered and
their disposal, during the last three years;
(e) how many ration dealers were
sentenced with imprisonment for
misappropriation/selling/diverting the items
in open market, during the last three years,
year-wise;
(f) the measures taken by Government
to check the malpractices;
(g) Government's nine point action plan
for tackling diversion of PDS items and its
implementation; and
(h) whether PDS has failed in the
country?
Sanction of new rail line projects in
Rajasthan
*263. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has not

83
accepted the proposal of some new rail
line projects because of paucity of funds;
and
(b) in view of the poor railway network
in Rajasthan, whether Government are
going to accept the projects i.e., to link
Bhiwadi to Delhi-Ahmedabad broad gauge
railway line, Jaisalmer to Sanu, Jaisalmer
to Barmer, and Jaipur to Nathdwara for
industrial, mining and tourism development
of the State?
Wasteful expenditure due to lack of
comprehensive planning
*264. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Comptroller and Auditor
General has pulled up Railways for lack of
comprehensive planning which resulted in
wasteful expenditure on track renewal
works on sections identified for gauge
conversion and the improvement in track
parameters is not commensurate with large
number of track renewal works undertaken
by Railways;
(b) whether CAG noted that the
budgetary control mechanism was
inadequate as seen from the savings over
some zonal railways and excess expenditure
over other during the same financial year
for the last five years both under divisional
and special railway safety fund; and
(c) what action his Ministry has taken
on the CAG's report?
Non-payment of arrears by sugar
mills in Uttar Pradesh
†*265. SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the sugar
mills in Uttar Pradesh under public sector,
cooperative sector and private sector owe
an amount of rupees 13445.41 lakhs,
9313.77 lakhs and 26413.78 lakhs
respectively for the price of sugarcane for
the season 2006-07;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
sugar mills under private sector in Uttar
Pradesh owe an amount of rupees 8455.02
lakhs for the price of sugarcane for the
2004-05 season and the seasons prior
thereto;
(c) if so, the steps taken by Government
to expedite the payment to farmers; and
(d) by when the farmers would get the
full payment?
Banned drugs in circulation
*266. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of drugs which
are banned globally, are being sold in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether some drugs which are
banned in the country, are still available in
the market; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

84
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken in this regard?
Quota under Tatkal Reservation
System
†*267. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of berth quota fixed
for reservation out of the total number of
berths under Tatkal Reservation System;
(b) whether the number of general
reservation berths has not been reduced
following implementation of Tatkal
Reservation System;
(c) if so, whether reduction in number
of general reservation berths has not
compounded the problems of passengers;
and
(d) the total additional revenue to be
generated by Tatkal Reservation System
for Railways?
Notification on establishment of
PCPIRs
*268. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL:
SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PATEL:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to refer
to answer to Unstarred Question 1995
given in the Rajya Sabha on the 16th March,
2007 and state:
(a) whether the policy for establishment
of PCPIRs has been notified by
Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, by when it would be notified?
Scarcity of steel products
*269. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:
(a) whether despite India being the
world's fifth largest steel producer there
has been scarcity of steel products in the
country;
(b) whether integrated steel plant sector
claims that the reported scarcity of steel is
man-made and has caused unregulated
imports;
(c) whether the Cold Rolled Steel
Manufacturers Association of India has
accused major steel plants of jacking up
the prices of hot rolled steel; and
(d) if so, Government's comments
thereon?
Aid from UK
*270. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the UK Government has
announced a new aid package of Rs. 2,000
crores for India over the next five years
which would be used mainly for improving
the country's health programmes and access
of the poor to healthcare;
(b) whether any concrete programme
of action plan for its use has been
considered;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether members of a large British
Healthcare Mission, during visit to India
have shown keenness to expand into the
Indian market and form joint ventures to
either set up distributorships or
manufacturing facilities in the country?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

85
Private sector participation in rail
projects
*271. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to invite private sector to
participate in railway projects in the
country;
(b) if  so, which are the areas the
Railways have identified for the private
sector participation; and
(c) whether his Ministry has ensured
to maintain public sector character when
private sector is allowed?
Mahoba-Khajuraho and Lalitpur-
Satna rail lines
†*272. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the State
Government of Madhya Pradesh has sent
a proposal to his Ministry regarding the
completion of railway line from Mahoba
to Khajuraho and Lalitpur to Satna;
(b) if so, the progress made, so far, in
this regard; and
(c) by when this railway line is expected
to be completed?
Amendment of the Consumer
Protection Act
*273. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
amend the Consumer Protection Act;
(b) if so, the essential features of the
proposed amendments;
(c) whether consumer forums below the
level of districts are proposed by
Government; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Poor quality ration supplied through
PDS
*274. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: W ill the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether serious complaints have
been received from various States about
the poor quality ration being issued
through the Public Distribution System,
particularly for those below the poverty
line;
(b) the details thereof for the year 2007,
so far, State-wise; and
(c) the action taken/proposed to be
taken by the Central Government to
remedy the situation and for taking punitive
action against those responsible therefor?
Standard of medical education
*275. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the committee of
academicians and scientists set up after the
Commission on Macroeconomics and
Health, co-chaired by the Finance and
Health Ministers, suggested that standards
of higher medical education needed to be
raised and monitored and recommended a
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

86
Postgraduate Medical Education Board for
higher education in medicine;
(b) if so, what are the other main
recommendations made; and
(c) how many of them have been
accepted by Government?
Late running of trains
*276. SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRI MAHMOOD A.
MADANI:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Indian Railways have
any norms/guidelines regarding the late
running of passenger trains;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether his Ministry conduct
recurrent surveys on the late running of
passenger trains;
(d) if so, what is the methodology
adopted in conducting such surveys and
the reason for such recurrent delays;
(e) whether Government identified the
railway divisions where the maximum
delays have taken place alongwith the
details thereof;
(f) what steps are being taken to
minimize the delays;
(g) whether Government propose to fix
accountability in this respect;
(h) if so, the details thereof; and
(i) if not, the reasons therefor?
Agricultural distress zones
*277. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to identify
agricultural distress zones in each State by
the Central Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
AIDS cases in NCR
†*278. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA:
SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn towards burgeoning HIV
positive (AIDS) cases in NCR;
(b) if so, whether Government would
draw a comprehensive policy for
prevention of AIDS;
(c) whether Government have taken any
steps to make people aware about AIDS;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Failure to provide basic health care
*279. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that our health
system has failed to provide basic health
care facilities in some parts of the country;
(b) if so, which are those parts and
whether it is also a fact that much promised
First Referral Units (FRUs) are virtually
non-existent and round the clock Public
Health Care (PHC) are either non-functional
or lacking to deal with pregnancy cases;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

87
(c) whether there is any plan/scheme to
improve the said situation; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Resentment among farmers for low
sugarcane price
†*280. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ : Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether any assessment of the
production of sugarcane this year has been
made;
(b) whether it is a fact that huge
quantity of sugarcane crop has been burnt
by the farmers because of not getting
payment for sugarcane from sugar mills and
also not getting proper price for sugarcane;
and
(c) if so, the efforts being made by
Government to check its recurrence?

————
List of Questions for  WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 155

Farmers’ indebtedness
1984. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether indebtedness of farmers is
increasing day by day and in some States it
has reached up to 60 per cent;
(b) if so, what are the figures of farmers’
indebtedness, State-wise;
(c) whether Government would provide
package to indebted farmers throughout the
country particularly to the farmers of Uttar
Pradesh who are waiting for their dues to
be cleared by the sugar factories; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Supply of milk products at DMS
depots
†1985. SHRI VINAY KATIYAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the supply of products such
as pure ghee, butter-100 gm, curd and sweet
milk apart from milk has been discontinued
in the depots of Delhi Milk Scheme;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether there is any scheme for
restarting the sale of the said items; and
(d) if so, by when it would be done?
Number of DMS employees
†1986. SHRI VINAY KATIYAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any plan to reduce
the number of employees of the Delhi Milk
Scheme; and
(b) if so, by when it will be done?
Loss of livestock due to mechanised
slaughter of animals
†1987. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are worried
about the fact that thousands of healthy
animals mostly Bovine, are taken to the

460
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
mechanised slaughter houses of
metropolitan cities and other countries
from many States where their killing is
banned;
(b) if so, what steps have been taken to
stop/to get stopped this continuous loss
of livestock;
(c) whether any project is being run by
the Central Government itself for the
protection and utilization of animals;
(d) if not, whether any assistance is
being provided to the projects running in
the States; and
(e) whether there is any provision to
provide assistance to States; if so, the
details thereof for the last three years?
Farm subsidies
1988. DR.  K. KESHAVA RAO: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that developed
countries like the US and Japan are giving
30 per cent of their GDP towards farm
subsidies;
(b) whether it is a fact that a country
like India where about 63 per cent depend
on agriculture is extending a scarce share of
the GDP towards subsidies; and
(c) if so, what steps Government would
take to step up farm subsidies to reduce
interest rates for agriculture and self-help
groups?
Subsidy for Vidarbha cotton growers
†1989. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Members of Parliament from Vidarbha in
Maharashtra have submitted a
memorandum in which they have
demanded subsidy for cotton growers and
to increase the purchase price for their crop;
(b) if so, the action taken in this regard;
and
(c) the arrangements made by
Government to povide subsidy to the
cotton growers in the event of crisis and to
increase the purchase price for their crop
in future?
Corporate farming
1990. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are lots
of shortcomings while promoting corporate
farming in the country;
(b) if so, Government's response
thereto;
(c) whether Government are taking any
initiatives for making long term transparent
policies for making corporate farming
successful in the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
details of steps taken or proposed to set
up strong systems to monitor contracts
and corporate farming so as to avoid
exploitation of the workers/growers and
farmers in the country?
Combating hunger through
investment in agriculture
1991. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Director-General of

461
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
FAO of the UN has recently commented
while in India that India needs to strengthen
its efforts to combat hunger through more
investments in agriculture;
(b) whether India has succeeded to
reduce its share of hungry people from 39
per cent to 20 per cent;
(c) whether according to FAO statistics
for the year 2006, one in four persons
remained hungry in India as compared to
one in five in China; and
(d) what are the steps being taken to
increase investments in agricultural sector?
Declining fertility of soil
†1992. SHRI SURENDRA LATH:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether fertility of soil is constantly
declining in the country;
(b) if so, the steps being taken to deal
with this problem;
(c) whether the production per hectare
is declining in comparison to earlier years
despite use of good quality seeds,
fertilizers, etc.;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether Government are providing
any help to the farmers to meet the losses
incurred due to above situation; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Adverse effect of global warming on
agriculture
1993. DR. BARUN MUKHERJEE:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the FAO
(UN) chief has recently predicted a huge
loss of cereals production of India due to
climate change;
(b) if so, whether Government agree to
it and what is Government's assessment in
this respect;
(c) which of the cereals may be worst
affected;
(d) whether Government agree that such
adverse effect of global warming is a matter
of great concern, particularly when India's
growth rate in agricultural sector has
alarmingly gone down; and
(e) what measures are being taken to
combat such adverse situation?
Awareness and extension centres for
poultry
1994. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to introduce regulatory measures
to govern the health of poultry livestock to
prevent from spread of diseases;
(b) whether there is also a proposal to
launch an awareness programme in the
poultry sector;
(c) whether more poultry research
institutes and extension centres would be
established to improve the quality of
poultry;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps proposed to finance and
assist small and marginal farmers to develop
and sustain poultry?

462
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Subsidy for sugar cultivation
1995. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether sugar cultivation in
Karnataka is facing setbacks this season
owing to unprecedented slump in the price
of sugar from Rs. 1600 per quintal to
Rs. 1200 per quintal;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether under similar circumstances
in the past, Government extended support
in the form of buffer stock subsidy, export
subsidy, etc., to the affected States;
(d) if so, the details of such support
extended by the Centre to different States
during the last three years, year-wise and
State-wise;
(e) whether the Government are
considering to extend the same support to
Karnataka; and
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Privatization of Delhi Milk Scheme
†1996. SHRI VINAY KATIYAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any plan to hand
over Delhi Milk Scheme to some private
companies;
(b) if so, by when; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Adulterated fertilizers
1997. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large
quantity of adulterated fertilizer is being
distributed and sold in Madhya Pradesh
which causes hardships to the farmers; and
(b) if so, what is the monitoring
mechanism proposed by Government to
the States when allotment of fertilizers is
made by the Central Government through
their agencies?
Increase in the milk prices
1998. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
milk is the best to recover from physical
exercise of day long labour by the poor;
(b) if so, whether Government, on the
other hand, are regularly increasing the cost
of milk in the Capital to the disadvantage
of the common people; and
(c) if so, the reaction of Government on
this matter?
India's position in agricultural
production
†1999. SHRI AJAY SINGH
CHAUTALA: W ill the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the position India
occupies at present in the field of
agricultural production in the world;
(b) the position of India in terms of
production of wheat, rice, cotton and pulses
in the world;
(c) the details of the steps being taken
by Government during the two years of
2007-08 and 2008-09 to make India a
frontline country in the field of agricultural
production;

463
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) whether Government have adequate
stock of foodgrains; and
(e) if not, the reasons which are
responsible for this shortage of foodgrains,
and the steps proposed to be taken to meet
this shortage?
Soil testing in Vidarbha, Maharashtra
†2000. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether soil test has been conducted
by the Department of Agriculture of the
Maharashtra Government in the villages of
Vidarbha area, so that cultivation can be
done as per the properties of soil of that
region;
(b) if so, the outcome thereof;
(c) whether suitable cultivation
according to the soil of Vidarbha has not
been started till date; and
(d) if so, by when new crop pattern
will be started?
Damage of crops by fog, hailstorm,
etc. in Northern India
2001. SHRI D HARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that potato, wheat
and vegetable crops have been damaged in
Northern India due to fog and heavy
hailstorms;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government propose to
provide any assistance to farmers whose
crops have been damaged and if not, the
reasons therefor?
Special schemes for production of
wheat, rice, etc.
†2002. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has selected
hundred districts for running special
schemes to increase production of wheat,
rice and pulses in the country;
(b) if so, the details of the scheme; and
(c) the details of selected districts,
State-wise?
Assessing implementation of package
for suicide victims
†2003. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had constituted a Task Force under the
chairmanship of Shri R. Radhakrishnan to
assess the implementation of a scheme
formulated for providing economic package
of Rs. 17,000 crores to farmers declared by
the Prime Minister as a result of suicide by
the farmers;
(b) if so, when this Task Force was
constituted;
(c) whether this Task Force has
submitted its report to Government; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Farming in plains and hilly areas
†2004. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the amount of assistance to be given

464
for per acre farming in plains by Central
and State Governments and the amount
required for farming in hilly areas as
compared to the above;
(b) whether his Ministry has prepared
any action plan for making farming in hilly
areas useful; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Corpus fund for farmers
2005. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to create a
corpus fund for assisting farmers affected
by crop loss;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
MSP of paddy, oil seeds and pulses
2006. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are proposing
to enhance the minimum support price
(MSP) of paddy, oil seeds and pulses for
the year 2007-08;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the request of the State
Government of Andhra Pradesh to increase
MSP for paddy from the existing Rs. 580/-
to Rs. 660/- per quintal for common variety
and from Rs. 610/- to Rs. 725/- for grade-A
variety of paddy has been acceded to;
(d) if so, the details pertaining to MSP
of paddy, oil seeds and pulses for the year
2007-08; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Short-term credit for farmers
2007. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government with the help
of any existing law have allowed for
negotiable warehouse receipt systems
which enable farmers to use grain as
collateral for short term credit and help them
to avoid immediate post harvest, low price
sales;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any measures have been
